run.procedureSummary: 1. Charge: add each cycle's charge to each crucible, ignoring capacity. 2. Overflow: walk crucibles 1 to 6 in order; any amount over capacity moves into the next crucible before that crucible's turn, so it can cascade; crucible 6's excess goes to slag. 3. State: a BASE crucible at or above its upper mark becomes SUPERHEATED; a SUPERHEATED crucible at or below its lower mark becomes BASE; otherwise no change. This uses the quantities after overflow, and each crucible is checked once. 4. Bleed: every amount is worked out from the quantities after overflow, using the states from step 3, before anything moves. BASE loses floor(q/4) to slag. SUPERHEATED sends floor(q/2) to the crucible before it (position i-1); crucible 1's goes to slag. Everything then moves at once. A crucible pushed over capacity stays that way until the next cycle's overflow; after cycle 5 it stays as is. 5. Tap: if the line total after bleed is strictly above 38, each crucible keeps floor(q/2) and the rest goes to slag. At exactly 38 it does not fire.

openPoints.point: Which states the bleed uses (before or after the step 3 update)
openPoints.assumption: The states after step 3. Step 3 finishes on all six before step 4 starts.

openPoints.point: Which quantities the bleed amounts come from
openPoints.assumption: The quantities after overflow, all fixed before any transfer ("figured before anything moves"). A crucible that receives a return flow still bleeds based on its own pre-bleed quantity.

openPoints.point: Whether overflow can cascade within one pass
openPoints.assumption: Yes. Excess lands in the next crucible before that crucible's turn, so the incoming excess counts toward its own overflow check.

openPoints.point: Crucible over capacity after the bleed
openPoints.assumption: No overflow inside the same cycle. It carries into the next cycle's step 2; after cycle 5 it stays over capacity (crucibles 2 and 4 end at capacity 8 and above 6 respectively: 10/8 and 7/6).

openPoints.point: Which total the tap test uses
openPoints.assumption: The sum of all six quantities after the step 4 bleed. Material already in slag does not count.
No. States change only in step 3. The tap is applied after step 3, so a state is not re-evaluated after a tap until the next cycle's step 3.

openPoints.point: Whether state is assessed at the start, before cycle 1
openPoints.assumption: No. Everything starts BASE and the first state check is step 3 of cycle 1.
Always floor (round down) on non-negative integers, for both bleed amounts and the tap's halves. The rounding remainder of the tap goes to slag.

run.balanceCheck: Starting melt 20 + charges (20+15+17+24+18 = 94) = 114; end melt 38 (6+10+9+7+4+2) + slag 76 = 114. Balanced.
run.notes: I ran the arithmetic with a Python script at C:\Users\Jaket\AppData\Local\Temp\om\desk-250\sim.py and checked cycle 1 by hand; it matches. Slag by source: overflow from crucible 6 is 1+3+8 = 12; BASE bleed plus crucible 1's return flow is 1+4+6+5+2 = 18; taps are 21+25 = 46; 12+18+46 = 76. Cycle 5 ends at exactly 38, which is the boundary case: the tap does not fire because the rule is strictly over 38. At the end, crucible 2 holds 10 against a capacity of 8 and crucible 4 holds 7 against a capacity of 6. Both got there from return flows in the cycle 5 bleed, and the write-up says they stay that way after cycle 5.
